div.head: The History of Abba Marcus Who Lived in Holiness on the Mountain of Tharmaka

div.ab: The blessed Serapion related to us, when he was in the remote district which is in the inner desert of Egypt:

While I was sleeping with Abba John, the aged, I saw in a dream two brethren, monks, blessed by Abba John. They said to him, Who is this that is sleeping here? He told them Abba Serapion. One said to his comrade, Arise, Let us go in and be blessed by him. But Abba John said to them, He just came in from the desert and he is very tired. Let him rest a little. They said: It is now some time that he has been living in humility in this desert and he has not yet gone to Abba Marcus who is in the mountain of Tharmaka. For he has no equal among all the monks who dwell in this desert. He is one hundred and thirty years old, and for ninety years no one has seen him; but forty days hence there are coming Fathers who are in the abode of life and they will take him home with them.

When the two brethren said these things I, Serapion, awoke. I saw that there was no one with Abba John. And I said, Thus I saw in my dream, O Abba. He said to me, Surely this was a true vision from God, but I do not know where this mountain is. I said to him, Pray for me. And when he had prayed, I bade him farewell and I was blessed by him.

I travelled to Alexandria, for I was a journey of twelve days from there. Because of the terror of that vision which I had seen, for several days I took no food. When I went through that terrible desert, in the heat of the day, the sun set on fire the very dust of the earth.

When I came to Alexandria, I asked one of the merchants
who travelled in distant places, saying. Tell me, my lord, in what country is the mountain of Tharmaka and how far off is it? The merchant said to me, The mountain of Tharmaka is forty days distant and it is at the entrance of Ethiopia beyond the sea of the Cathayans. I said to him, How shall I go there? He said to me, If you travel by water, it will not be very far for you, but if by land through the desert it will be a long way.

When I heard these things, I took a small jug of water and a few dates and I committed my soul to God. I travelled through that desert forty days. I saw no animals and no birds because there was no possibility of living there for animals or birds. Moreover there was no rain or dew in it. After forty days the water which I had gave out, and I was in great distress. I did not have strength to go on, but that vow which I had made to the Messiah to whom I had committed myself would not permit me to turn back.

When I cast myself upon the ground as dead, behold, these two brethren whom I had seen in my dream when I was in the cell of Father John, came and stood over me and said to me, Were you not waiting for us to go with you? Arise by the strength of our Lord. When I arose, I saw one of them looking at the ground, and he turned to me and said, Do you need a drink of water? I said to him, Yes, Abba. He showed me a root called qamus and said to me, Eat this root and proceed by the strength of our Lord. When I ate a little of it, immediately I perspired as if I had been dipped in water. My soul was strengthened, my face assumed a joyous expression, my limbs gained alertness and I was as if I had never made a journey. They showed me a path by which I should go to the saint.

I arose and journeyed through the desert for seven days.
Then I reached that mountain and I ascended it until I reached the top. There was nothing on that mountain; also, it was such a steep mountain that, to speak after the manner of men, it seemed to reach as high as heaven. But I reached the top of the mountain in three days. A great sea was underneath the base of the mountain. I travelled on it (i. e. the mountain) for seven days and saw nothing.

One night I saw the angels of God descending to that saint, and they were singing praises and saying, Blessed are you and good is your soul, Abba Marcus. Behold, we have brought that Serapion whom your soul desired to see. Moreover, you have not desired to see anyone else of mankind. When I heard these things, I was in great fear and I proceeded toward that sight to the cave of Abba Marcus.

When the angels went up to heaven, I drew near to the door of the cave and I heard the voice of Abba Marcus reciting a passage from the holy scriptures, and he was comforting himself, saying, A thousand years in your sight are as yesterday when it is past. (Ps. 90:4). Blessed are you, my soul, because you have not wallowed in the mud of this world. Blessed are you my body, because you have not reveled in the desires which beget filthy imaginings. Blessed are you, my eyes, because Satan has not been able to blind you in vile vision and he has not turned you aside to gaze upon beauty which has blinded saints. You have not looked on the mirrors in which demons dwell, and by which they hunt the beautiful ones who are the daughters of Eve. Blessed are you, my ears, because the jackal-voice of women of the world has not howled in you, and you have not been troubled by the confused rumours which are counsels of Satan. Blessed are you, my hands, because you have not given and taken in
the business of Satan. My nostrils have not been filled up with the fragrance of slander, and my feet have not run in the ways which lead to destruction. My thoughts have not flown after vanities. My soul has been satisfied with the life of the spirit. My body has been sanctified by the splendour of angels. My eyes have been enlightened by the vision of the children of light. My ears have been purified by the hearing of those who are holy. My nostrils have been filled by the incense of fragrant herbs. My hands have been sanctified by the cross which was formed by stretching them out (in prayer). My feet have been blessed by bending the knee and standing in service. My thoughts have been purified by meditation about that spiritual land. Bless the Lord, O my soul, who forgives all your iniquities (Ps. 103:3). Why are you distressed, my soul, because you are not taken from this guard of demons? The powers of Satan will not be able to condemn you. There is no impurity of sin in you. Do not be grieved, my soul, for you have not been defiled with filthy mire. Be not afraid, my soul, because they will not seize you when you pass through the guard of demons.

When he had recited many passages from the holy scriptures, he went outside the door of the cave. As I was weeping sadly, he called to me, saying, You are come in the peace of the Messiah, Brother Serapion. May God give you a reward for the labour of your feet. Brother Serapion, draw near, my son, and greet your aged father. When I drew near to him, he embraced me with both arms as a man in the strength of youth. As he was weeping and kissing me, he said: The fragrance of my son is as a spiritual fragrance. (Cf. Phil. 4: 18, Gen. 8: 21.) Verily, my son, have you taken all this trouble to see this old man?
My son, for ninty-five years I have not seen any other person. My son, I did desire to see you for many years.

When I had entered his cave, he said to me, Behold, my son, for thirty-five years I have been in this cave. My eyes have not seen a living thing. I have eaten no human bread. I have not worn clothing of (this) world. For thirty years I have been here in great distress from hunger, thirst, nakedness, and conflict with devils. I even ate dust, my son, from hunger. I drank water from the sea from thirst. Thirty years of severe peril have passed over me. I have been in great tribulations. Sometimes myriads of demons who were in the sea lay in wait for me that they might drown me. Frequently they dragged me from here to the base of this mountain until there was no skin or flesh left on my limbs. They shouted at me and kept saying: Go away from our land and from our place. Not since our days has any one else come here. But I endured patiently for thirty years through hunger, thirst, nakedness, and conflicts with demons until finally the mercy of God rested upon me. He commanded my body and the hair grew until it weighted down my limbs with its weight. A continual supply of spiritual food from the Lord was sent to me. Angels descended and ascended by me. I saw the realms of the kingdom and the habitations of the souls of the saints. I saw the blessedness which is promised to the righteous. I saw the paradise of God. He showed me that tree from which Adam and Eve ate. I saw Enoch and Elijah alive. There was nothing which I sought from God which he did not show me.

When he told me these things, I said to him: Abba, how did you come here? He said to me, I was a native of the city of Athens and I was absorbed in the study of
philosophy. When my parents died, I said, I shall die also like my parents; but I will leave the life of the world of my own free will before they take me by force. Immediately I stripped off my garments and threw myself upon a board in the sea, and I was cast upon this mountain. When he had told me these things, it was morning. I saw his body, and I began to tremble for I was in great fear, because he was not like a man, but rather only something which was speaking like a man. When he saw that I was afraid he said to me, My son, do not be afraid of this corruptible body, woven within a corruptible web.

Again he said to me, My son, is the world continuing to prosper as in former times? I said to him, Yes, Abba, the world is more prosperous now than it used to be. He said to me, My son, does heathenism still hold authority and are Christians persecuted? I said to him, By the help of your prayers, persecution of the Christians has ceased. There is no heathenism at the present time, all the leaders of the country are Christians and the kingdom of the Christians holds sway.

He rejoiced with great joy when he heard these things and he said to me, My son, are there holy men in the world who work miracles, do marvellous things, raise the dead, open the eyes of the blind, cleanse lepers and heal the sick? (cf. Matt. 10:8) as our Lord said, If you have faith, as a grain of mustard seed, you shall tell this mountain to remove hence . . . and it shall remove. (Matt. 17:20). When he uttered this word, that mountain was lifted up from the earth about five ells, and suspended in the air, and it began to fly toward the sea. He smote it with his hand and he said to it, I did not tell you to depart, stay where you are and be quiet! I fell on my
face from fear. He said to me, Have you never seen a miracle like this? I said to him, No, my lord. Thereupon he sighed and wept, and said to me, Woe to the land in which there are Christians in name only and not in deeds. Blessed be the Lord God who brought me out to this land that I should not die in the home of my parents.

When it was evening, he said to me, Brother Serapion, is it not time to make an oblation of love? I did not answer him a word. He arose and stretched out his hands to heaven and recited this psalm. The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want (Ps. 23:1). He turned to me and said, My son, the table, He has prepared. Thereupon I said to him, Excuse me, Abba. But he said to me, Come, my son, let us enjoy what God has sent to us. I marvelled and I was seized with dizziness, for there was no one inside the cave and there was nothing in it.

When we entered within the cave, I looked and saw a beautiful table prepared, with two chairs in place, bread, white as snow, beautiful choice fruits, two great fish roasted with fire, fine vegetables, olives, dates, and a large waterpot filled with water. When we sat down he said to me, Say grace, brother Serapion. But I said to him, Excuse me, Abba. Then he said, Blessed is my Lord. I saw, as it were, a hand of fire stretched out and it drew a cross over that meal. When we had eaten he said (to the table), My son, remove from here. Immediately that table was taken away. In all my life, I have never consumed food which was as pleasant and enjoyable as that, or drink as enjoyable as that.

He answered and said to me, Brother Serapion, behold how God loves his saints. Every single day he sends me a fish but to-day because of you God has sent us two.
Every day, my brother, God thus sends to me spiritual food and spiritual drink. For thirty years, I was in this mountain eating dust from hunger and drinking foul water from the sea. I went naked and barefoot until the skin was worn off from my limbs and my flesh was scorched by the sun and I was prostrate upon the ground as dead. Demons fought with (i.e. against) me. They were dragging me along the ground and torturing me. God permitted me to be persecuted by them for thirty years while I was tormented by hunger, thirst, and nakedness. Moreover, I did not see a single animal or bird which might have comforted me. Behold I have been here ninety-five years to-day in (all of) which my eyes have not seen any of the creatures whom God created, except demons only. But when that period of thirty years was finished, when I was in great perils of affliction, God commanded my body and the hair grew until all my limbs were covered. From that time on, the evil spirits were not able to touch me, no hunger or thirst overpowered me, and I did not become sick or weak. Now, behold, the allotted time of my life is completed and God has sent you that you may bury this poor body with your holy hands.

When he had told me these things, on the fifth day (Thursday) at eventide, after we had taken that nourishment, he said to me, Brother Serapion, forgive me if I trouble you a little this night with the service of song. When we had completed the first service and recited all the Psalms in three hours, he said to me, Sit down, my brother. When we both had seated ourselves, he said to me, My brother Serapion, as soon as my body is buried, stop up the entrance to this cave and go in peace, but do not remain here. Then I began to weep and to shed passionate tears,
and I said to him, Please (lit. yes), my father, ask of God and he will take me with you to wherever you are going. He said to me, No! By the Messiah, the son of God, I do not know whither I am going. Then he said to me, Do not weep in this day of my gladness, for that one who brought you will guide and lead you. But your departure will not be by the way in which you came. Brother Serapion, this day is the greatest of all the days of my life. To-day, my brother, my soul will reach that desirable dwelling, and will enter and find rest in those spiritual habitations with the souls of the righteous. To-day this weak body will find rest from pains and sicknesses. To-day I will attain to that abode of life.

When he said these things, that cave was filled with light which was brighter than the dazzling rays of the sun. I was enveloped as though by the radiance of the sun and I was aflame with the brilliance and the fragrant incense of the odours. He held on to my hand and raised me up, saying, Come in peace, O ministers of the living God. Behold Gabriel and Michael are standing outside, let us go out to them. Then he sealed that cave with the sign of the cross and he said, Remain in peace, O temple which sheltered me in exile. In you I will leave this body, which was sheltered in you during life, until the resurrection. And you, O body, habitation of distresses, remain in peace. The Messiah, for whom you endured hunger, thirst, nakedness, and cold, will clothe you with glory in the day of his coming. Remain in solitary peace in which there is no sound. Remain in peace, O dwelling of my soul. Remain in peace, O my eyes, sleep and rest. Remain in peace, O my hands, which have toiled in the service of the vineyard of the Messiah. Remain in peace, O my feet, which were blessed by glorious standing in worship.

When he said these things and I was weeping passionately, a voice was heard which said, Bring to me the chosen vessel from the earth: bring to me the worker of righteousness; bring to me the perfect Christian; come, Abba Marcus; come, rest in the land of life. He turned and blessed me, saying, Remain in peace my brother Serapion. May the Messiah give to you an excellent reward for your labours; blessed are you, my brother. Now, remain in peace, this mountain; and all the earth and those who dwell in it; security and peace, and prayers be to the holy church. Amen. My true brother Serapion, by the Messiah, the son of God, I adjure you not to take anything from this poor body, not even one particle of hair. Do not bring clothing to clothe it except this hair with which God clothed it. Do not pass the night here from evening, for it was then the last hour of the night. Then he said to me, Let us kneel in prayer, my brother. When we knelt in prayer, I heard a voice which said, Spread out your wings and bear (him) away.

When I heard these things I arose and looked upward, and I saw his soul being borne by angels. It was clothed in a white stole, and they were ministering to it and going up with it. The veil of this air was drawn back and I saw the guard of demons standing ready, and I heard a voice which said, Flee, children of the darkness, from before the light. His soul was detained a moment; and one of the evil spirits raised his voice and cried: Up, and go for the confounder of demons. But when his soul passed by all the hosts of demons, immediately I saw as it were a likeness of a hand of fire which was stretched out to him and I did not see him again.

I performed the service over that holy body until morning,
then I bore it and put it in that cave, and I stopped up its entrance with stones. I prayed and went down from that mountain, supplicating God that he would send me help that I might go out from that terrible desert.

At eventide, when the sun was setting, behold those two blessed ones whom I saw with Abba John, came to me and said to me: Truly you have buried to-day a body of whom this world was not worthy, cf. Heb. 11:38. Arise and let us go in the cool of the night because you will not be able, in the daytime, to go in this desert. I went with them until dawn. When it was dawn, they said to me, Go in peace, and pray for us.

When they had departed from me, I looked and saw, and behold, I was standing at the door of the cell of Abba John. I was in great amazement and I praised God. When I was offering my praise, Abba John came out at the sound of praise and he said to me, You are come in the peace of the Messiah, Abba Serapion. When I had entered his cell and related to him all these things, he praised God and said to me, Truly, we are Christians in name and not in deeds!
The end of the history of Abba Marcus who was in the mountain of Tharmaka.
